subject: Request: modular private-offer packaging & channel margin for Stratus.ai
messages:
From: Elliot Tsu <elliot.tsu@stratus.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stratus.ai
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace private offer packaging question

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo last week — Stratus.ai is excited about faster inference for our large-model inference pipeline. Procurement asked me to follow up with a couple of specifics for the AWS marketplace private offer we're considering:

- We need the offer to support a modular SKU: Reserved node-hours (monthly), burst node-hours (metered), and an embeddings-only SKU. Can you confirm whether Redwood can create a bundled private offer that allows our customers to mix and match SKUs and report consolidated usage to our billing system?
- Channel margin: our reseller partners need a clear % pass-through for commissions (target 12% net to partner). We also need visibility on how list-price vs committed discount waterfalls affect partner net.
- Pricing cadence: can list prices be fixed for 12 months and have a pre-agreed quarterly true-up?

We also attached our procurement requirements PDF. Can you share an initial packaging suggestion and a private-offer price sheet (ballpark) for internal review?

Best,
Elliot
Head of Procurement, Stratus.ai

[attachment: stratus-map-requirements.pdf]

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Tsu <elliot.tsu@stratus.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer packaging question

Elliot — thanks for the clear summary and attached requirements. Quick responses inline and a proposed next step:

- Modular SKUs: yes — we can model the private offer as a multi-line private-offer package on AWS (reserved node-hours line, metered burst line, embeddings line). Usage is consolidated via our usage export so Stratus can map to your billing system.
- Channel margin: we can present a gross-to-net waterfall showing partner commission as a % of list price or of net revenue; the partner-facing pass-through you described (12%) is feasible in the structure but will change effective net to Redwood depending on the committed discount.
- 12-month list-price freeze with quarterly true-up: doable; we'll add a true-up clause that reconciles net effective price vs committed usage.

Next step: I attached a preliminary price sheet (redwood-pricing-v1.xlsx) with two packaging options (A: higher commit / lower list price; B: lower commit with higher partner pass-through). Can Ben and Camila review for margin impacts, then I'll turn this into an AWS private-offer draft.

—Olga
Director, Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference

[attachment: redwood-pricing-v1.xlsx]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer packaging question

Olga — looked at the sheet. A couple notes for the private-offer negotiation:

1) If partner commission is defined as 12% of list price, and we give Stratus a 30% committed discount, partner net will indirectly be larger relative to our realized revenue. Recommend structuring partner commission as 12% of net (post-commit discount) to stabilize Redwood net.

2) For the embeddings-only SKU, we should consider a separate list-price ladder (per-1000 embeddings) instead of tying it to node-hours to avoid skew when customers have heavy embedding but low generation usage.

3) Add a clause limiting cross-SKU crediting (i.e., prevent customers from converting all reserved node-hours to embeddings at the lower per-unit price).

I can run a margin sensitivity quickly if you want. Jordan — can you confirm procurement docs we require to formalize the private offer?

—Ben
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2029 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer packaging question

Ben — for procurement we'll need:
- Signed SOI (statement of intent) or PO from Stratus with committed node-hours and committed term
- Approved reseller commission statement (legal sign-off for pass-through mechanics)
- List of reseller partner entities who will receive commissions (for marketplace contract mapping)

I captured those in a short SOI template and attached (SOI-acceptance-draft.docx). If Stratus is ok with net-based partner commission we can include language that keeps partner % fixed while protecting Redwood margin.

I'll also note that AWS private-offer line-items can carry custom attributes — we should use those to flag which SKU lines are allowed to be pass-through eligible.

-Jordan
Head of Deal Ops

From: Elliot Tsu <elliot.tsu@stratus.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stratus.ai, Maya Rios <maya.rios@contracting.io>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2029 10:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer packaging question

Thanks — this is very helpful. A few follow-ups from procurement after internal review:

- Stratus prefers partner commission to be a % of the chargeable line (post-commit discount applied) to ensure partners aren't advantaged by our list-price maneuvers. We understand that affects Redwood gross. Can Redwood provide a margin-protection corridor (e.g., minimum net effective price floor) so you don't go below an internal threshold?
- For the embeddings SKU, we want a per-1K-unit price with a cap for burst overage to avoid runaway billing.
- We also want a clause that allows Stratus to reallocate up to 15% of monthly reserved-hours to burst-hours with automated conversion at a blended rate.

Can you provide: (1) one-page summary with the final commercial approach we just discussed, and (2) an updated pricing sheet showing the margin-protection corridor and blended conversion example? We can then send the SOI.

Elliot

> - List of reseller partner entities who will receive commissions (for marketplace contract mapping)
>
> I captured those in a short SOI template and attached (SOI-acceptance-draft.docx). If Stratus is ok with net-based partner commission we can include language that keeps partner % fixed while protecting Redwood margin.
>
> -Jordan

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Tsu <elliot.tsu@stratus.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2029 16:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer packaging question

Elliot — attaching a one-page commercial memo and updated pricing workbook with the margin-protection corridor and a worked blended-conversion example (see sheet 'BlendExample'). Highlights:

- Commission mechanics: structure A (partner % of net) — partner receives 12% of net revenue post-commit discount; Redwood guarantees a minimum net floor equal to 60% of list price for reserved node-hours and 45% of list price for embeddings (this is the corridor we can sign to). Corridor can be adjusted if Stratus increases committed volume.
- Blended conversion: example shows monthly reserved-hours reallocation up to 15% converting to burst at a blended rate (70% reserved rate + 30% burst rate), with automated billing tags to keep reporting clean.
- Embeddings: per-1K pricing with burst cap mechanism (we implement a soft cap that triggers pre-alerts at 80% and an overage cap policy).

If that aligns, please send the signed SOI and a list of reseller entities. We will prepare the AWS private-offer draft and route to legal for the reseller pass-through statement.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if you want to walk the corridor math together next week.

—Olga

[attachments: redwood-pricing-v1.xlsx, SOI-acceptance-draft.docx]
